UN peacekeeping chief says talks on future of Lebanon mission must begin soon
item.description:
By Maya Gebeily

BEIRUT, Oct 14 (Reuters) - UN peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix on Wednesday urged the UN Security Council to begin negotiations on the future of peacekeepers deployed in Lebanon, as Beirut campaigns for an extension to the mandate set to expire at the end of this year.

A UN peacekeeping force known as UNIFIL has been deployedin southern Lebanon since 1978 but the Security Council last year ordered the mission to begin withdrawing at the end of 2026.

item.title: Two ships sink near Hormuz after being hit by projectiles amid surge in attacks
item.description:
By Jonathan Saul and Renee Maltezou

LONDON, Oct 14 (Reuters) - A container ship and a dry bulk carrier have both sunk near the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday.

Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month.

item.title: Pilgrims caught up in Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
item.description:
By Timour Azhari

RIYADH, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Pilgrims in Saudi Arabia to visit Islam's holiest sites may not have anticipated being caught up in an air war, but some experienced an attack by Yemen's Houthis first hand and others have been forced to change their plans.

Footage of the massive blast that killed 13 people and wounded 300 in a Riyadh airport departure terminal struck by a Houthi missile on Saturday showed many passengers attired in the simple white clothes of Muslim pilgrims travelling to Mecca.

item.title: Houthis say targeted Saudi oil giant Aramco, vow more attacks
item.description:
Yemen's Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in an area housing the energy giant's operations centre.

Powerful explosions also rattled Riyadh, as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted a missile fired by the Iran-backed group towards the capital.

item.title: Saudi league postpones three matches after Houthi attacks
item.description:
The Saudi Arabian football league (SPL) has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr, following the dramatic escalation in the country's war with the Houthis.

The matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for "logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches", according to a statement published on Tuesday on the SPL's website.
